summary:
SpaceTrace is a web app that compares six under-recognised Earth sites with the Moon and Mars targets they could stand in for. For each pair it calculates a Planetary Analog Similarity Index (PASI) from four values (slope, hottest temperature, coldest temperature and dryness) and grades the match across eight dimensions, from geology to operations. Every number is labelled by origin, such as NASA data or a cited estimate, and every site has an Evidence panel with sourced facts and links. A Search Earth map screens 185 land areas on climate alone to suggest where else to look.

This answers the challenge by searching Earth for places that could serve as analogs for other worlds, and by making each choice transparent and checkable. It matters because analog sites are where missions rehearse before they go, so planners need to know how good a match is, and how well we know it. SpaceTrace is a screening tool, not a verdict.
 We chose six sites on purpose: each one has eight dimensions graded and its facts traced to named sources, and we preferred well-evidenced comparisons over a long list with thin data. We favoured under-recognised sites, including several in India. Search Earth covers breadth with a climate-only screen of 185 areas.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
SpaceTrace helps people choose and understand Earth analog sites for the Moon and Mars. It pairs six under-recognised sites with the targets they could stand in for: Lonar Crater, El Malpais Lava Tubes and the Deccan Traps (Moon), and Tso Kar and Puga Valley, Chott el Djerid and Movile Cave (Mars). For each pair the app shows a split map (Earth imagery beside the Moon or Mars), a scored report card, an Evidence panel of sourced facts, and credited photos. A Search Earth map screens 185 land areas on climate alone to suggest where else to look.

HOW IT WORKS
Overall match = (PASI + Dimension match) / 2. PASI, the Planetary Analog Similarity Index, is the plain average of four similarities (slope, hottest temperature, coldest temperature, aridity), each 1 minus the absolute Earth-target difference divided by the factor’s range. Dimension match grades eight dimensions (geology, terrain, temperature, water and ice, dust and erosion, biology, caves, operations) as Strong, Partial or Weak, using the data-based similarity where we have it and published literature for the rest. The Methodology tab shows every formula and input.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT
Analog choices are often made from reputation or convenience. SpaceTrace gives planners, educators and students a transparent, checkable way to compare sites and to see how well each number is known. It points attention to sites that get less coverage, including sites in India (Lonar, Deccan Traps, Tso Kar and Puga Valley), and it makes the limits of each comparison visible, so the tool supports discussion and does not replace expert judgment.

WHAT IS CREATIVE
Honesty is built into the interface. Every input is labelled by origin (NASA data, cited value or estimate), every site has an Evidence panel with named sources and links, and data completeness is reported next to the score. At Lonar, an independent satellite surface-temperature check is shown in the Evidence panel next to the climate figure used in the score. Search Earth turns the same scoring idea into a planet-wide first-pass screen.

DATA AND TOOLS
Earth temperature and rainfall: NASA POWER (2025). Earth slope: AWS Terrarium elevation tiles, built from NASA SRTM and other open elevation data. Imagery: NASA GIBS, Moon Trek and Mars Trek. Moon references: LRO Diviner and LOLA studies. Lonar cross-check: MODIS MOD21A1D via NASA AppEEARS (not used in the score). Built with React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet and Recharts. Photos are credited on each page, and all sources are listed in the NASA Data and Other Data fields.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED AND LIMITS
We separated measured inputs from estimates. Some Mars reference values (Terra Sirenum, Pavonis Mons) and the Jezero slope are estimates, and geology and cave grades are literature ratings; the app says so. NASA POWER is a reanalysis averaged over about 50 km, so it describes a region and not a single spot. Search Earth ignores terrain, geology and caves, so it is a shortlist and not a verdict. We left out photos whose licences we could not confirm.

USE OF AI
Claude (Anthropic) and Gemini (Google) were used as coding and research assistants for the app’s code, evidence summaries, slides and this text. The team reviewed the data and sources. No images or video were AI-generated.
